image_description: A side-profile view of a large American bison standing on a gravel path next to a grassy field. The animal has a massive, shaggy dark brown forequarter with a prominent shoulder hump and a lighter, less furred hindquarter. In the background, there are mountains and sparse trees under a blue sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible in profile; it appears broad and massive. While the horns are partially obscured by the thick fur of the forehead, the general shape and size are consistent with a bison.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, dark beard of long hair hangs from the chin and throat area, clearly visible against the lighter neck fur.
The eye is visible as a small, dark point on the side of the head, consistent with the species.
Ears are not prominently sticking out; they appear small and are largely concealed by the dense mane/fur around the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits the characteristic heavy build, appearing significantly taller at the shoulders than at the hips.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a very clear, large hump at the shoulders covered in thick, shaggy dark brown fur, matching the taxonomy perfectly.
The rear section of the body transitions to shorter, smoother hair compared to the front, exposing the underlying muscle structure more clearly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although partially hidden, the visible horn tips are short and curved, proportional to the massive head and body.
The legs are thick and sturdy. While the hooves are slightly obscured by the angle and ground texture, the leg structure is anatomically correct for a bovid.
The tail is visible hanging down, ending in a distinct dark, bushy tuft of hair.

The visual evidence matches the taxonomic prior knowledge without deviation.
